title: Bondy–Chvátal edge-closure lemma for Hamiltonicity
statement: Let $G$ be a finite simple graph on a vertex set with $n$ vertices, and let $u$ and $v$ be two distinct, nonadjacent vertices of $G$ whose degrees satisfy $\deg(u) + \deg(v) \ge n$. Then $G$ is Hamiltonian if and only if the graph $G + uv$, obtained from $G$ by adding the edge joining $u$ and $v$, is Hamiltonian.
hypotheses_covered: finite graph (Fintype V, n = number of vertices)

Let $G$ be a simple graph and let $u$ and $v$ be nonadjacent
vertices in $G$ such that
\[d(u) + d(v) \geq \nu \qquad (4.5)\]
Then $G$ is hamiltonian if and only if $G + uv$ is hamiltonian.
